turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files describing perovskite solar cells as
complete devices — `substrate` (glass + transparent electrode), `etl`
(electron-transport layer stack), `htl` (hole-transport layer stack),
`backcontact` (metal / carbon back electrode), `deposition` (absorber
deposition procedure; `>>` separates steps). Every candidate below uses the
same MAPbI3 absorber in the same n-i-p (regular) architecture; they differ
only in the remaining columns. Each row is a device CONFIGURATION whose
efficiency is the median over at least 3 independently fabricated cells, so
it is a reproducible recipe rather than a single champion cell:
  - b3_pvk_stack_train.csv: 300 configurations with the measured power
    conversion efficiency (%).
  - b3_pvk_stack_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE configurations whose power
    conversion efficiency (%) was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and
    the same device columns.

Using the training data, select the 5 candidates with the HIGHEST power
conversion efficiency (%).

Reason from the device physics — band alignment and selectivity of the
transport layers, interface recombination, contact chemistry and the film
quality the process is likely to give — then end your answer with an
explicit ranked list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902,
c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
# Reasoning from device physics

For MAPbI3 n-i-p cells, the top-performing configurations in the training data share clear physical signatures. Let me identify what drives high PCE:

**Highest-efficiency training patterns (>18%):**
- Compact/planar SnO2 or TiO2-c ETL with an *additional* passivating/electron-selective interlayer (SnO2-np, C60, PCBM, BaSnO3)
- Well-matched HTL: Spiro-MeOTAD (proven, deep HOMO ~–5.2 eV), or PTAA
- **Au back contact** (best HTL/metal work-function alignment, minimal reaction; Ag can corrode via iodide migration)
- Clean spin-coated stacks, no exotic scaffolds

Champions: `TiO2-c | SnO2-np / Spiro / Ag` (20.85), `TiO2-c / Spiro / Au + evap` (19.5), `TiO2-c | PCBM / PCDTBT / Au` (19.35), `TiO2-c | BaSnO3 / PTAA / Au` (18.9), `TiO2-c / PHPT-py / Au` (18.7).

**Key selectivity rules:** bilayer ETLs (compact + passivating np/C60) beat single layers; standard HTL (Spiro/PTAA) with Au beats novel/unknown HTMs with reactive contacts; carbon and "none" HTL configs cluster low-to-mid.

# Screening the pool against these rules

- **c064** `TiO2-c | SnO2-np / Spiro-MeOTAD / Au` — near-identical to the 20.85% champion (only Ag→Au, actually *better* contact). **Top candidate.**
- **c005** `TiO2-c | PCBM-60 / PCDTBT8 / MoO3|Au` — twin of the 19.35% PCDTBT1 device; MoO3|Au is an excellent hole-collecting stack.
- **c068** `SnO2-np | TiO2-np / PTAA / Au|MoO3` — dual-oxide ETL + PTAA + Au/MoO3, matching the PTAA/Au high-performers.
- **c025** `SnO2-c | TiO2-np / Spiro / Ag` — bilayer SnO2/TiO2 ETL + Spiro; strong analog to 16.7% SnO2|C60 and 17.3% ZnO|SnO2 devices, benefiting from cascade band alignment.
- **c031** `SnO2-c | SnO2-mp | TiO2-c / Spiro / Au` — triple metal-oxide selective cascade with Spiro/Au; strong selectivity, good contact.

Others considered: c017 (evaporated TaTm/C60 tandem-style stack, ~17.9% analog) is credible but Ag contact; c077/c056 (SnO2/Spiro/Au) solid ~14–18% but single ETL; c045 (TiO2/PTAA/Au) good. The five above best combine passivating bilayer ETL + proven HTL + optimal contact.

# Final ranking

Final: c064, c005, c068, c025, c031
